ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A one-turn rectangular conducting wire frame abcd wound from the same kind of wire of uniform thickness is fixed and motionless, in which there is a magnetic field (not drawn) in the rectangular region efcd, the direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil, the magnitude B of the magnetic induction intensity changes uniformly with time t, and $\frac{\Delta B}{\Delta t}=k$ (k>0). It is known that ab=fc=4L, bc=5L, and the resistance of a conducting wire of length L is r. Find the current in the conducting wire frame abcd.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A one-turn rectangular conducting wire frame abcd wound from the same kind of wire of uniform thickness is fixed and motionless, in which there is a magnetic field (not drawn) in the rectangular region efcd, the direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil, the magnitude B of the magnetic induction intensity changes uniformly with time t, and $\frac{\Delta B}{\Delta t}=k$ (k>0). It is known that ab=fc=4L, bc=5L, and the resistance of a conducting wire of length L is r. Find the current in the conducting wire frame abcd.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an outer rectangular conducting wire frame, the top side is ab, the right side is bc, the bottom side is cd, and the left side is da; a is at the upper left, b is at the upper right, c is at the lower right, and d is at the lower left. Inside the rectangle there is a horizontal dashed line from the left side e to the right side f, and the dashed line ef divides the outer rectangle into upper and lower two parts. The problem text states that only in the lower rectangular region efcd is there a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the coil. Reasoning: From the given ab=fc=4L and bc=5L, it can be known that the width of the magnetic-field region efcd is equal to the width ab of the outer rectangle, 4L, and the height is fc=4L, so the area of the magnetic-field region is S=4L×4L=16L^2. The conducting wire frame has only this one turn of outer rectangular wire abcd, the wire is of uniform thickness and the same material, and the resistance of each length L is r. The total length of the outer frame is 2(ab+bc)=2(4L+5L)=18L, so the total resistance R=18r. The rate of change of magnetic induction intensity is ΔB/Δt=k, therefore the magnitude of the rate of change of magnetic flux through the wire frame is S·k=16kL^2, and the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is |ε|=16kL^2. By Ohm's law, the magnitude of the induced current in the conducting wire frame is I=|ε|/R=16kL^2/(18r)=8kL^2/(9r).
